meaning: w: side of the square window, in px at 1/4 photo resolution (a leaf is ~35 px across), in which the leaf share around every pixel is measured. This density map only draws the zones: a small window follows single leaves, a large one draws smooth rings around the dense core.
l: how many density groups (airy ... dense) the plant is split into, by k-means on the density of its leaf pixels. 1 = one density for the whole plant.
m: smallest zone, in px (a leaf is ~1000 px). Smaller pieces are merged into the zone around them, so the zones don't fall apart into specks.

e: lowest density that still counts as plant. Where the density map is at least this, the pixels belong to the plant area (leaves plus the gaps between them); below it is background. A lower edge makes the outer zones reach further out, with more gaps, so their leaf share is lower.

c: highest leaf share f a zone may have when it is turned into layers, layers = -ln(1 - min(f, cap)). It limits how many layers a nearly solid zone counts: 0.85 = 1.9, 0.90 = 2.3, 0.95 = 3.0, 0.98 = 3.9 layers. The only setting that doesn't change the zones themselves.
